reference.title: Band Standing Reverse Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen; the band is hardest at the top of the curl, where it is stretched most
prescription.progression: Band tension is user-chosen: pick a band you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then a stronger band or a shorter grip on the band.

cues.text: Stand on the middle of the band, feet hip width, one end under each foot; hold the ends with an overhand grip (palms facing back), hands beside the thighs.
Breathe out and curl up, elbows by your sides, knuckles leading.
Squeeze with the hands at chest height; wrists straight, knuckles up; the band is tightest here.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band, 2-3 s, to straight arms.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bending down (knuckles dropping) as the hands come up
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists straight, in line with the forearms; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the hips to stretch the band
mistakes.fix: Lighter band; stand tall with the glutes and abs braced.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
mistakes.fix: Elbows stay by the sides; only the forearms move.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hands down
mistakes.fix: Take 2-3 s to lower to straight arms.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Pronated grip: biceps activity in the lifting phase was about 19% lower than with the supinated grip, so the brachioradialis and brachialis share more of the work (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Elbows stay near the sides; a small forward drift at the top is normal (clinical opinion)

Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest where the band is longest; at matched effort, elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity in upper-body exercises (Andersen 2010); with a band under the feet the load rises toward the top of the curl
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

sources.title: GymVisual #15511, Band Standing Reverse Curl, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)
Marcolin et al. 2018, differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl (PeerJ 6:e5165; PMC6047503)
Oliveira, Matta, Alves, Garcia and Vieira 2009, effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Elbow or wrist pain: use a lighter band and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
The overhand grip is weaker than the palm-up grip: start with a light band.

Check the band for nicks or tears before each set and make sure it cannot slip off its anchor (under the feet, round the upright). Stand firmly on its middle so it cannot slip out from under the feet.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort with the palms down: turn the hands toward a neutral (hammer) grip.
Too hard at the top: step on the band with one foot only.
progressions: Stronger band, or feet wider on the band.

muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis and the wrist extensors (mapped to the forearm extensor region): with the palms down the brachioradialis takes a larger share of the elbow flexion and the wrist extensors hold the wrist straight; biceps activity was about 19% lower than with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis and the wrist extensors (mapped to the forearm extensor region): with the palms down the brachioradialis takes a larger share of the elbow flexion and the wrist extensors hold the wrist straight; biceps activity was about 19% lower than with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Still flexes the elbow, though its activity was about 19% lower than with the supinated grip (Coratella 2023); the brachialis (not a separate id on this rig) works hard whatever the grip.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Still flexes the elbow, though its activity was about 19% lower than with the supinated grip (Coratella 2023); the brachialis (not a separate id on this rig) works hard whatever the grip.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder as the bar rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder as the bar rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so the hips do not swing the hands up.

phases.label: Bar on the thighs, overhand grip

guides.label: Bar arcs up to chest height
Elbow bends through a full range
